region: El Dorado County · Sierra Foothills, California
about: Rombauer Vineyards was founded in Napa Valley in 1980 by Koerner and Joan Rombauer; Koerner’s great-aunt Irma Rombauer wrote The Joy of Cooking. Best known for its Chardonnay, the family has also made Zinfandel from the Sierra Foothills since the mid-1990s, when Koerner began farming and buying grapes there. In 2010 they bought the Twin Rivers Vineyard in El Dorado County, and in 2019 the former Renwood winery in neighbouring Amador County, where the Zinfandels are now made.

Twin Rivers sits on a granite plateau about 1,650 feet up in the foothills, with sandy, decomposed-granite soils, warm days and cool nights, conditions the family is restoring it to exploit as a high-elevation Zinfandel site. Grapes are picked at night to hold acidity, destemmed, optically sorted and cold-soaked, fermented in tank and basket-pressed, then finish malolactic fermentation and age in a mix of American and French oak, only about a tenth of it new.

Expect a ripe, generous Zinfandel at close to 16% alcohol, in the plush style Rombauer is known for. Wine Spectator rated the 2022 91 points, describing jammy raspberry and blackberry with cinnamon, licorice and bittersweet chocolate over briary tannins, and suggested drinking it through 2031. Its richness and spice stand up well to smoke and char, which makes it a natural match for meats from a wood fire.
